evidence: Windows Rust probe: RelPath::parse("safe/C:/outside") succeeds, to_path_buf yields C:outside with a Disk(C) prefix, and join_to replaces the project root; zircon_runtime/src/asset/project/paths.rs:313-315 passes the result to create_dir_all
impact_or_question: A manifest asset root can resolve outside the owning project root on Windows and create directories there.
next_action: Reject a platform prefix in every parsed component and require project-root containment before filesystem writes; add Windows regression coverage.

evidence: Windows probe: validate_project_name(COM¹) and validate_project_name(LPT².txt) return Ok while COM1 is rejected; Microsoft Win32 Naming Files, Paths, and Namespaces lists COM¹/²/³ and LPT¹/²/³ with extensions as reserved
impact_or_question: Creation requests and portable manifests accept Windows reserved device names that cannot be used as ordinary project directories.
next_action: Recognize superscript device suffixes before accepting a project name and add cross-platform name-contract tests.

evidence: The public load_project_manifest_value_from_toml_str entry has no MAX_PROJECT_MANIFEST_BYTES check; current Hub Summary and Runtime callers bound bytes before calling it.
impact_or_question: A new direct caller could parse an oversized manifest before the shared byte budget is enforced.
next_action: Decide whether the shared public parse entry should enforce the byte budget itself and add a direct-entry test.

evidence: windows_project_session_mutex_name hashes the supplied path UTF-16 bytes; Hub and Editor canonicalize their project roots separately, with no cross-host equivalence test for extended prefixes or non-Unicode paths.
impact_or_question: Equivalent physical project roots may produce different mutex names if callers pass different lexical forms.
next_action: Add a Hub-to-Editor cross-host mutex-name equivalence test and define the required canonical root form.
